A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same readable 33-page CAML paper, including Appendices A–N. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content except for first-page presentation changes and Figure 5 legend corrections.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on four PDE benchmarks, component ablations and optimizer comparisons in Section 6, plus additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, optimizer comparisons, sensitivity analyses and failure-case experiments.

M1.justification: CAML's aligned constraints, analytic or Newton-based offset calculation, and residual-delay schedule are unchanged. Section 5, Appendices D–E and Algorithm 1 match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Heat, Poisson, Navier–Stokes and Helmholtz with the same domains and boundary conditions. The supplementary Poisson scenarios in Appendices G, H and M also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain PINN, L∞-PINN, SA-PINN, BRDR and DB-PINN; optimizer and learnable-bias comparisons also match. Figure 5 corrects 'DP-PINN' to 'DB-PINN', which was already identified in v1's Section 6.1 and Tables 2–3.

E3.justification: Backbones, optimization settings, training budgets, accuracy thresholds, metrics and unsuccessful-run criteria are identical. The detailed configurations in Appendix I, Tables 8–14, are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, loss-landscape and optimization-dynamics analyses, computational-overhead measurements, learnable-bias comparison, parameter sensitivity study and failure experiment are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five initialization seeds in Section 6.1 and the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Table 2. Run-count and uncertainty information throughout the appendices also matches.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, empirical curves and qualitative solution visualizations are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Figure 5 changes only legend labels; its plotted results remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 4.1, Lemma 4.2, and the assumptions, proofs and offset derivations in Appendices A–D are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about loss-valley geometry, gradient conflicts, aligned constraints, residual delay, and improved PINN convergence and stability.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability limits are unchanged, including degeneration under pure Neumann conditions without zeroth-order terms, limited gains in benign landscapes, and the future extension to time-dependent PDEs.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, hyperparameters, PyTorch and GPU information, computational timings and the CAML code-access link are unchanged. Appendices D–E and G–M provide the same technical details.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the bibliography are unchanged. The positioning relative to adaptive losses, conflict-aware optimizers and hard-constraint methods remains the same.

P1.justification: Small textual edits update the arXiv version/date and correct Figure 5's 'DP-PINN' and 'L∞ PINN' labels to 'DB-PINN' and 'L∞-PINN'. Body prose, section organization and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a small camel icon beside the title, slightly adjusts first-page spacing and corrects Figure 5's legend. Plot geometry, captions, tables and all other page layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 5's DB-PINN label makes the curve attribution consistent with Section 6.1 and Tables 2–3, providing a small clarity improvement. The scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged; the title icon and version/date updates are cosmetic.
